name: Abi-albon
overview: Abi-albon was a male warrior known as the Arbathite and was listed as the twentieth member of 'the thirty,' a distinguished group of David's mighty men. The Bible records him briefly without mention of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His inclusion among David's elite fighters highlights his role in the king's military exploits.
namesAndTitles: The name Abi-albon means '[my] father is Albon,' indicating a personal or familial connection to someone named Albon. Another name associated with this individual is Abiel, meaning '[my] father is God [El],' though this is a separate proper name referenced in a different passage. Neither name is recorded as being divinely given.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Abi-albon beyond what is indicated by his name's meaning. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text regarding his kin or descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Abi-albon's significance lies in his membership among the thirty mighty men who served King David, underscoring his valor and trusted position within David's military leadership. Though details about his life are scarce, his mention in the biblical record affirms the importance of faithful warriors who supported God's anointed king during a pivotal era in Israel's history.
